authority_boundary.note: This normalized graph is a consumer read model. Every item returns to its ToS source_refs.

explanation.ru: Статус объявлен исходной записью; это не текущий допуск предмета.
explanation.en: The source record declares this status; it is not a current admission of the subject.

explanation.ru: Отсутствие заявления об эквивалентности не доказывает различность предметов.
explanation.en: No equivalence claim does not establish that subjects are distinct.

explanation.ru: Полярность не заменяет исходную формулировку, оговорки или оценку; отсутствие поля не означает положительность.
explanation.en: Polarity does not replace source wording, qualifications or assessment; an absent field is not positive.

explanation.ru: Сохранён исходный статус; словарь не оценивает обоснованность утверждения.
explanation.en: The source status is retained; this vocabulary does not assess the assertion.

explanation.ru: Исходный статус рассмотрения не равен текущему допуску. Решения, область использования и отзыв читаются отдельно.
explanation.en: The source review status is not current admission. Decisions, allowed use and withdrawal are read separately.

accepted_with_limits.ru: В записи отмечено: принято с ограничениями

explanation.ru: Видимость метаданных не выдаёт права на содержимое, публикацию или новое использование.
explanation.en: Metadata visibility grants no content access, publication or new-use rights.

explanation.ru: Ссылка сохраняет предмет контекста; она не подтверждает утверждение и не объединяет его с другим предметом.
explanation.en: The reference preserves the context's subject; it neither endorses the assertion nor identifies it with another subject.

label.ru: Отдельная оценка предмета и её ограничения

explanation.ru: Допуск формы не означает принятия её предмета; сохранены отдельные решения и отзывы.
explanation.en: Form admission does not endorse its subject; separate decisions and withdrawals are retained.

explanation.ru: Снимок не является текущим разрешением исполнения, доступа или публикации.
explanation.en: The snapshot is not current execution, access or publication permission.

explanation.ru: Язык формы и язык источника различаются; перевод или адаптация не выводятся из языка интерфейса.
explanation.en: Form and source languages differ; translation or adaptation is not inferred from the interface language.

explanation.ru: Точная механическая привязка остаётся в исходном контексте.
explanation.en: The exact mechanical binding remains in the source context.

explanation.ru: Значение сохранено буквально; эта форма не объясняет и не переоценивает его.

property_definitions.definition: The source-attributed composition scope of this exact Claim; not a global fact, completeness proof, historical chronology or admission.
The source-attributed declared composition coverage of this exact Claim; not a global fact, completeness proof, historical chronology or admission.
The source-attributed membership basis of this exact Claim; not a global fact, completeness proof, historical chronology or admission.
The source-attributed declared ordering of this exact Claim; not a global fact, completeness proof, historical chronology or admission.
The source-attributed ordering basis of this exact Claim; not a global fact, completeness proof, historical chronology or admission.
The source-attributed composition limitations of this exact Claim; not a global fact, completeness proof, historical chronology or admission.
The source-described research purpose of this persistent corpus; exact membership, order and admission remain separate Claims.
The source-described selection criterion of this persistent corpus; exact membership, order and admission remain separate Claims.
The source-described corpus coverage account of this persistent corpus; exact membership, order and admission remain separate Claims.
Whether the exact referenced source record bytes are readable in this snapshot; distinct from truth, review and current-use admission.
Current or historical within the verified source package, only when that exact version is available. A historical record is not the current record or a current grant.
The researcher's proposed meaning for this comparison set; not an accepted Sign definition.
The explicit reason for comparing these occurrences, not automatic equality or recurrence.
The declared source extent of the proposal, not an exhaustive corpus claim.
An alternative account or explicit comparison limit; the field does not create counterevidence.
Unknowns and limits of the proposed interpretation, not an admission status.
The language whose specified lexical content is considered, not the wording language or interface language.
The proposed rendering language, not permission or proof that a particular translation exists.
The exact lexical use or reading considered; it does not quantify over every use of a word.
The intended receiving context, task and limits of the rendering judgment.
The stated semantic, pragmatic or other aspects considered; full transfer means only these aspects.
Adequate, inadequate or undetermined in the declared scope; independent of search, confidence and admission.
Full, partial, none or undetermined for the stated aspects; not universal equivalence or impossibility.
What is reported to survive the rendering, including explicit uncertainty or none known.
Reported losses, unexamined aspects and open alternatives of the scoped judgment.
Outcome only for the stated sought criterion and coverage; missing is not none found, and none found is not untranslatability.
What the reported search sought, which may be stricter than the considered partial renderings.
The attributed extent and unknowns of a search; neither exhaustive coverage nor an execution receipt is implied.
A reported procedure, if supplied; null stays unknown and this wording cannot execute tools.
The source endpoint's lexical usage scope; neither a source path nor the language of its description.
The target endpoint's lexical usage scope; its identity remains a separately typed Claim endpoint.
The declared source-endpoint language for a lexical comparison, not its statement language or an automatically attested Language identity.
The declared target-endpoint language for a lexical comparison, not permission to translate or a Language identity reference.
The source-described grounds and uncertainty of historical lexical ordering; not capture time or a normalized chronological key.
The source-described basis and limits of lexical cognacy; not proof of direct descent or an inferred common ancestor.
The specific use, task or interpretive context of a proposed lexical rendering, not universal equivalence.
Which aspects of the situated reading are proposed to survive this rendering; no completeness or acceptance follows.
Source-declared limitations, losses and unresolved alternatives of the proposed lexical correspondence.
The described use at an exact bound source unit, including its uncertainty; not its lexical grouping or an accepted meaning.
The situated context and limits of the described use, distinct from the frozen source address.
A source-described lexical grouping and its limits, not a particular spelling or accepted normalization.
A source-qualified grammatical account; unknown or competing analyses remain explicit.
A source-qualified lexical reading, not an automatically accepted philosophical concept.
The declared interpretive context and limits in which this reading is investigated.
The stated scope and boundary of the reading, preserving ambiguity and unknown alternatives.
A source-described written representation and its limits, not proof of occurrence or grammatical analysis.
The source-declared written-form identity field, distinct from the language and script of its description. No occurrence or language attribution is inferred.
The source-declared written-form identity field, distinct from the language and script of its description. No occurrence or language attribution is inferred.
The source-declared written-form identity field, distinct from the language and script of its description. No occurrence or language attribution is inferred.
The source-declared written-form identity field, distinct from the language and script of its description. No occurrence or language attribution is inferred.
A source-grounded description of the language as a research referent, not a code or one written realization.
A described linguistic variety; dialectal or historical relationships require separate Claims.
The linguistic, social or historical criterion and its limits, not a universal test separating languages and dialects.
A source-grounded description of a writing system or explicitly scoped writing tradition, not a spoken language.
Whether the referent covers a particular sign repertoire or broader tradition; no timeless universal sign reading is implied.
A source-described notation and mapping convention, not a translation or an executed text transformation.
What the convention represents, leaves ambiguous or omits; reversibility requires evidence, not the scheme name.
The declared language of the classification term, including und when unknown; not the language of the classified work, source quotation or interface.
The declared script of the classification term; null remains unknown and does not determine a source's original script.
The attributed classification term in its declared language; it is neither a type ID nor a universal vocabulary entry.
The source-declared criteria or grounds for this classification, not an accepted proof.
The specific object, realization or passage and contextual limits to which the classification applies.
The technical media type declared for these exact file bytes by a source-item manifest; not detected format validation, literary genre, communication medium or permission to read the payload.
A source-attributed account of reception or its historical change, not an evaluation by ToS.
The particular people, community, practices and limits for which this historical account is made; not universal recognition or absence.
The documented practices of reading, response or transmission distinguishing the process; similarity alone does not establish influence.
The criteria and practices by which the historical community distinguishes an authoritative or exemplary repertoire.
Whose authority and which field this historical canon concerns; no ToS admission, correctness or universal consensus is implied.
What supports a decline or interruption in this receiving context, including surviving counterexamples and limits; database absence alone is not evidence.
For whom access or attention was renewed and what remained known or transmitted elsewhere; not the first discovery by anyone.
The source-described continuity, transformations and gaps supporting this legacy; resemblance does not establish a direct causal chain.
Source-described modern reconstruction, collation or arrangement; not the ancient referent. Required in the descriptive composite profile; native witness records retain their own source fields.
Reported editorial operations and their limits, not admission or executable code. Required in the descriptive composite profile; native witness records retain their own source fields.
Source-described extent and omissions, not an assertion of complete survival. Required in the descriptive composite profile; native witness records retain their own source fields.
The source-described textual portion and its uncertainty, not a transcription or physical artifact.
How this research distinguishes the textual portion; an editorial number does not settle original boundaries.
The particular quoted passage and attribution limits, not a general reference to a work.
Source-reported position and boundary limits; a bibliographic locator is not a resolved exact-text anchor.
Complete, fragmentary, not extant or unknown as attributed by this Claim; not certainty, admission, physical custody or access permission.
What occurred within the declared biographical scope.
Why the episode is documented as relevant to a life, with limits; significance is not causal proof.
The activities or circumstances identifying this phase, including discontinuities.
Why this research distinguishes the phase; dating and the subject's identity remain separate Claims.
The historical developments or configurations by which this periodization is described.
The research criterion, spatial scope and limitations of this periodization; rival periodizations may coexist.
The cohort as described by its source, without implying uniform experience or belief.
The specific generational criterion and its exclusions or uncertainty; individual assignment requires a separate Claim.
The scoped configuration of conditions, including what this description does not cover.
Source-described political conditions in the stated historical scope.
Source-described economic arrangements or constraints, not inferred personal wealth.
Source-described cultural practices and conditions, not uniform beliefs.
Source-described religious institutions or practices, not automatic personal adherence.
Source-described education and teaching arrangements, not automatic individual participation.
Source-described scientific practices, knowledge or technologies; availability does not prove use or influence.
The documented life condition within the stated scope.
What the source supports about the condition's relevance, distinguished from causal interpretation.
What the source cannot establish, including diagnostic and retrospective interpretation limits.
Documented bodily circumstances with attribution and uncertainty, not an unqualified diagnosis.
What this historical formation consists in, not a list of admitted participants.
The teaching or inquiry continuity distinguishing this school from an institution, a name or a general similarity class.
How the tradition is transmitted and reworked, including discontinuities; shared wording alone does not prove continuity.
The historically situated direction or undertaking distinguishing this movement from a school, tradition or mere collection of similar ideas.
The declared historical scope, distinct from the scope of an individual association Claim.
The contestable continuity criterion for this formation, not an identity decision by the reader.
The specific historical affiliation, transformation or articulation asserted, not an endorsement.
The source-declared grounds for this particular relationship, not an assessed proof.
The described relational dimension or activity, not a whole-life claim.
Source-owned historical scope wording, including unknown bounds; it supplies no normalized temporal key or capture time.
What holds this collective together; mere similarity of members is insufficient.
How membership is understood and where it is unknown or disputed; this is not a list of accepted members.
The continuing interaction or practice grounding this community, not proof of unanimous belief.
The organized roles and continuity by which this particular institutional body is described.
The stated extent and limits of this historical collective description, not a timeless definition.
The contestable criterion for retaining this collective's identity through description changes; names alone are insufficient.
What inquiry this method conducts and how; its description does not prove that it succeeds.
Declared conditions for applying the method. An empty list records no known conditions, not unconditional applicability.
What is done conceptually and what is not implied by doing it; no executable is selected.
Source-described prerequisites; an empty list means none recorded, not proof that none exist.
The conceptual movement or reframing, with its intended effect and limits.
The situation in which this movement is proposed to make sense; not universal applicability.
What is supposed for the inquiry; this is not a claim that the scenario occurred.
Conditions granted for examining the scenario, not accepted propositions; empty means none recorded.
Declared coverage of recorded assumptions; claimed completeness is not mechanically established.
What consequence or possibility is examined under the stated assumptions; it is not an unconditional conclusion.
What is presented imaginatively or figuratively and its stated scope.
The source account's characterization of the image, without imposing one aesthetic taxonomy.
The identified rhetorical arrangement and its role in the source, not a historical person or automatic interpretation.
The domain supplying the figurative presentation, not a bibliographic source locator.
What is interpreted through the figurative presentation; distinct from a software target or identity assertion.
Which aspects are proposed to carry across domains and which do not; this is an interpretation requiring assessment.
What is valued or used as a criterion of valuation, and in what sense.
Whose or which discourse's valuation is described; recording it does not adopt it.
The model or desired form and its limits; neither realization nor endorsement is implied.
How this account treats realization of the ideal, distinct from whether the description has been assessed.
What ontological commitment is described and under what substantive limits.
The source-described force, including conditional or suspended commitment; separate from assessment and admission.
What this perspective selects and leaves aside; the subject viewed through it is linked by separate grounded claims.
What is organized or distinguished by this category, within the declared philosophical scope.
The substantive tension or difficulty being investigated; its being recorded does not prove that all authors share it.
Why resolving or reframing this difficulty matters within the stated inquiry, not a compulsory project value.
What makes the grouped difficulties belong together while preserving their differences; membership is not inferred from spelling.
The interrogative content, including conditions and scope.
The presuppositions attributed to the question, or an explicit account of what is unknown. Recording them does not accept them.
The commitments or refusals that distinguish this stance, including uncertainty and limits.
In which respect the terms are differentiated; neither shared names nor graph separation supplies this criterion.
Why the terms are treated as opposed and with what limits; logical incompatibility requires its own argument.
The full proposition in this source account, including its conditions. Its presence does not assert its truth or endorsement.
Source-declared force of the proposition in this account, such as hypothetical or denied; separate from the truth and review of its description.
What reasoning is reconstructed and which limits remain; not an automatic interpretation of graph structure.
Partial, claimed_complete or unknown coverage of this argument. Claimed completeness is not mechanically proved.
The described inferential transition, not a proof that the transition preserves truth.
The source account's description of the reasoning mode; it does not select executable inference code.
What is challenged and why. Targets are separate grounded Claims; no negation of a target is inferred merely from a challenge.
The described scope and limits of this research referent; it is not a canonical definition, historical date, or causal assertion.
The explicit research criterion for retaining this semantic subject through corrected descriptions; shared names or equal record versions are not identity evidence.
Source-declared calendar, not an inferred conversion. A missing or null value is not Gregorian.
What the dating concerns. Historical time is separate from witness creation, data capture and knowledge revision.
Exact, approximate, uncertain or unknown date value. Exactness at the declared precision is not evidence that the enclosing Claim is true or accepted.
Original year-numbering declaration. Unsupported or unknown numbering is preserved without conversion to astronomical years.
Source-declared before, after, during or overlaps relative to a resolved anchor, not an inferred absolute date or causal edge.
Inclusive lower date key: astronomical year * 10000 + month * 100 + day, proleptic Gregorian only. Not a timestamp or duration; absent for unparsed or incompatible calendars.
Inclusive upper date key widened to source precision. Intersect [a,b] with start <= b AND end >= a. Missing bounds are unknown, not infinite.
Readable projected title; never an identity key.
Declared review state; not-recorded explicitly means no state was supplied, not acceptance.
Registered type closure, including this type. Contains selects a type and all its descendants.
Source-declared interval start; precision and calendar remain separate qualifiers.
Source-declared interval end; absent means unknown, not infinite.
Source-owned assertion version, distinct from entity identity and projection content revision.

types.definition: A scoped ordering of Works linked by exact contains_work Claim versions in an exact Collection version. Membership, coverage and historical chronology retain their own evidence; alternative orderings remain independent Claims.

A Claim-scoped account of the proper material parts of a physical artifact or fragmentary physical ensemble. Physical attachment, custody and restoration have separately evidenced relations and stated coverage.
An identifiable research selection with a stated purpose and continuity criterion. Exact membership and arrangement are asserted separately within their research scope.
A qualified Claim-scoped account of an intellectual object's proper parts, with explicit extent, local order and assessment scope.
A qualified selection of members of a research corpus, with partial, exhaustive-in-scope or undetermined coverage and independently declared order.
The complete, unexecuted merge or split plan inside one exact Claim. Execution and reference migration require a separately authorized transition.
A Claim-scoped proposal comparing the complete declared set of exact Occurrences. The Claim owns the candidate's identity and assessment; a Sign has its own issuance record.

A Claim-scoped account of rendering a specific lexical subject. Adequacy, transfer of particular aspects and reported search have separate descriptions; each value belongs to its Claim and stated scope.

An addressable written representation within an explicitly declared notation scope. Its form_identity fields preserve the exact represented string; a change to that referent follows the identity transition route.
A source-described linguistic system or variety. Language and dialect relationships are recorded as scoped, contestable Claims.

A persistent research referent for a language. Names, identifiers, scripts and particular utterances describe or relate to that referent. Corrections preserve its identity; splitting or merging referents records explicit lineage.
A source-described variety identified through explicit linguistic, social or historical criteria. Dialect and historical-stage relationships each retain their source-grounded Claims.
A writing system or explicitly bounded writing tradition. Historical sign repertoires have their own stated scope; a broad tradition such as cuneiform can be investigated at that broader level.
A source-described convention for representing source writing in another notation. Particular applications record their transformations, accuracy and reversibility separately.
A source-attributed expressive or documentary form, such as article, letter, lecture, aphorism or commentary. Form and genre are independently recorded facets whose terms may overlap.
A source-attributed carrier category of a physical artifact or bibliographic item, such as papyrus, codex or printed book, within the stated classification scope.
A classification value belonging to a qualified Claim, with an explicit term, basis and scope.
A source-attributed genre designation of an intellectual object within a stated classification context.
A source-attributed mode of communicating an intellectual object, such as spoken, written or performed expression, scoped to a realization or context.
Historical engagement, loss of attention, renewed access and continuing legacy within a declared receiving context.
A temporally developing, source-described engagement with earlier intellectual material within a declared receiving context.
A historically situated process of selecting or sustaining an authoritative or exemplary repertoire within a specified community or context.
A source-described decline or interruption of attention or transmission within a stated context and evidential scope.
A bounded episode of renewed access or attention for a specified receiving context.
A source-described, persisting configuration of later uses, practices or interpretations traced to earlier intellectual material. Specific claims of influence retain their own evidence.

A modern scholarly object reconstructing, collating or arranging evidence from physical or textual witnesses. Its members, representations and readings have separately identified records. Member and coverage observations retain their attribution and assessment status.

An independently addressable textual portion identified through a stated research boundary. Corrected descriptions preserve the referent; competing identifications remain source-grounded Claims. Carrier and exact text-unit evidence have their own references.

A particular passage described as quoting another text, identified by its containing context and position. Each quoting context identifies its own passage, with references to the quoted material and textual evidence.
A Claim-scoped report of textual survival for a specified intellectual object and an explicit scope of evidence.
A bounded occurrence described through its documented place in a person's life.
A source-described phase of a person's life identified through an explicit research boundary; it may encompass several events and processes.
A historically situated periodization identified through stated developments or configurations and a declared interpretive scope.
A source-described cohort identified by a declared relation of age, historical experience or generational self-understanding.
A scoped configuration of historically described conditions in one or more domains. Specific causal relationships require their own evidence.
A documented condition of a person's life, including bodily circumstances where relevant to the source account. Its relationship to philosophical content is examined through explicit evidence.
A source-described historical formation of intellectual inquiry, transmission or shared direction, with separately identified participants, doctrines and institutions.
A source-described historical teaching or inquiry formation with a specified lineage and scope of shared practice.
A historically traced continuity of reception, practice and reinterpretation across carriers and changes.
A historical intellectual current characterized by a specified direction of inquiry or change and its source-described scope.
A historically described collective constituted through specified social relations or joint activity.
A social group described through continuing shared practices, interaction or belonging, with its internal differences preserved.
A historically identified institution with organized roles and continuity. Its locations, buildings and intellectual affiliations have their own relations.
A source-described way of conducting inquiry with explicit applicability conditions.
A specified intellectual action within an inquiry, with its source-described prerequisites and purpose.
An identified, potentially reusable movement within reasoning or interpretation. Its form, justification and attested occurrences are examined separately.
An explicitly hypothetical scenario used to examine a question or consequence. Its assumptions retain their hypothetical force throughout the inquiry.
An identified imagined or figurative presentation within thinking or expression, with a stated source and interpretive context.
An identified arrangement or device of expression. The thought it presents and its effects on readers are described through separately grounded relations.
A rhetorical figure interpreted through a source-grounded mapping between domains in a specified use and context.
An identified object or criterion of valuation within a source-described context.
A source-described normative or aspirational model that may organize values. Claims about its realization in particular persons or states require their own evidence.
A specified commitment about what exists or has explanatory standing within a conception, method or hypothesis. Its stated conditions remain part of the commitment.
A specified perspective or dimension under which a concept or conception is examined within a stated reading.
A source-described organizing category of thought or being within a particular inquiry.
An identified tension or difficulty sustaining an inquiry, related to its interrogative formulations and proposed solutions.
A research grouping of distinguishable problems under an explicit criterion. Each membership relation has its own grounds and stated coverage.
An interrogative formulation with explicit presuppositions and scope. Several questions may articulate one problem; the standing of their presuppositions is examined separately.
An identified stance within an inquiry, described through commitments, limits and relations to theses or problems. Attribution to a person or source is a separate grounded Claim.
A specified differentiation made under an explicit criterion, with separately grounded contextual roles for its terms. The account states the respect and extent of their separation.
A distinction whose terms are presented as opposed in a specified respect and source context.

A proposition under examination, with its conditions and declared assertion force. Premise and conclusion are contextual roles within an inferential step; research assertions about the thesis are recorded as Claims.

A reasoning structure described or reconstructed from evidence, with explicit coverage. Inferential steps, target theses and objections have grounded relations; validity, soundness and attribution are assessed separately.

An identified transition in an account of reasoning, with premises and conclusions assigned contextual roles through Claims. Its premises, rule and result are open to examination; reconstruction order and historical chronology have separate evidence.
An identified challenge with substantive reasons, an explicit target and a stated scope. Its grounds and success are assessed in relation to that target.

A research referent with an explicit continuity criterion connecting different situated conceptions. Each conception retains its definition; membership is established through grounded, contestable Claims and explicit type assignment.

A situated account of thought with its own referent identity and substantive description. Attribution, conceptual membership and expression have separately grounded Claims. Historical transformations relate conceptions; descriptive corrections advance the record version while preserving the conception.

A persistent communicative or documentary intellectual object, with separately identified realizations, carriers and descriptive records. Corrections preserve its identity; shared content and identity attributions require their own Claims.

A document constituted as addressed correspondence, including an unsent draft. Sender, addressee, authorship, dispatch and reception are separately grounded contextual Claims and may remain unknown. Copies retain their identified carrier and document relationships.

A persistent physical source object, including a manuscript carrier. Its ID remains stable through descriptive corrections. Inventory records, intellectual content, scholarly composites, representations, custody and historical relationships retain their own references and Claims.
The family of source-described happenings, developments and persisting conditions in the historical world.

A source-described occurrence treated as one happening. Its identity is independent of labels, disputed dating, participants, and correction of its description. An interpretation of its significance is a separate claim.
A source-described temporal development whose phases, participants and relations to events are identified through grounded Claims.
A source-described persisting condition within an explicit historical scope.
An exact text representation bound to its source and version.
A source selector bound to an exact version of a representation; its offsets resolve within that version.
A source-layout or method-proposed unit carrying its unit kind, boundary status and exact source binding.

A particular source-bound use with a correctable research description and immutable native TextUnit binding. Its lexical form, Lexeme and sense have separately grounded relations. The unit retains its stated granularity and boundary status.

A persistent lexical research referent established through an explicit grouping analysis. Spellings, occurrences and senses relate to it through grounded accounts. Descriptive corrections preserve the subject; incompatible referents require explicit lineage.

A situated lexical reading retained as its own research referent. Sense-of and interpretation-of links are separately grounded Claims; descriptive corrections preserve competing readings and their identities.

An authored identity issued for an exact concrete candidate through competent source-visible promotion. Its immutable issuance basis records that historical act; current use follows the applicable admission. Descriptions and HumanForms retain the basis and its limits.
A retained native semantic-annotation-v2 sign with its original identity, record and admission status under that native profile.
A source-declared occurrence within a native semantic-annotation-v2 packet, preserving its identity, exact anchors, version and observed status under that native profile.
A source-declared lexical grouping within a native semantic-annotation-v2 packet, preserving its identity basis, version, source anchors and admission status under that native profile.
A source-declared lexical_sense within a native semantic-annotation-v2 packet, preserving its tos.sense identity, source basis, version and admission status under that native profile.
A versioned stand-off annotation or segmentation packet with explicit source references and assessment status.
Claim under the semantic annotation v2 contract, preserving proposition, evidence, maker, alternatives and review refs.
Evidence for an annotation claim with direction, role and exact source anchors.
A source-owned review event with explicit scope over claims or segmentations and a recorded assessment basis.
An addressable source relation assertion linked to its exact supporting claim.
The root for declared ToS entity families in the semantic interchange hierarchy.
An object whose ToS identity persists while versioned descriptions and assertions may change.
A persistent person-like responsibility bearer. Authorship, translation and editing are expressed through typed responsibility relations.
A persistent collective or institutional identity participating in source claims.
The family of persistent intellectual creations, communicative documents, realizations and aggregates, with the bibliographic ladder as one declared profile.
An abstract intellectual or artistic creation with separately identified realizations, editions, acquired items and files.
A language- or version-specific realization of one Work.
Root for edition and collection identities that embody or aggregate Expressions and Works.
A published or edited manifestation with separately identified acquired copies.
An aggregate publication or container with evidence-bearing membership claims.
One physical or digital acquired copy or container.
One immutable byte sequence addressed by its declared digest.
A versioned observation of an access or authority address, with an explicit reference to its target.
The family of authored ToS node classes, with each instance retaining its declared candidate or canonical status.
An authored node that anchors a semantic reading in a work, passage or other cited source.
A source-returnable concept node or an explicitly pre-canon concept candidate.
An authored node holding a reviewed, distilled claim and its source-bearing ground.
An authored lineage or movement path between semantic objects.
An authored node describing source-linked movement or change, with separately recorded temporal assertions.
An authored node describing a sustained condition within a source-linked route.
An authored support or contextual grounding node.
An authored node describing the setting needed to understand source-linked thought.
An authored node describing a reviewed image-bearing comparison and its interpretive scope.
An authored reviewed synthesis node.
A versioned assertion whose identity, evidence and review posture remain separate from its subject and object.
A reified evidence-bearing assertion with its own version, maker, provenance and review state.
Root for explicit temporal assertions, instants and intervals; raw period labels remain unparsed candidates.
A claim-scoped temporal value with an explicit calendar, facet, precision and uncertainty posture where available.
A normalized point-like temporal value within a declared calendar and precision.
A normalized start/end temporal value with separate boundary precision and meaning.
A claim-scoped publication, manufacture or distribution activity preserving literal statement, roles, places and time.
A value whose scope and reference are owned by its Claim.
A literal source statement of place, with normalization recorded through a separate Place reference.
Root for evidence, review, provenance and maker representations supporting claims.
A source-returnable evidence reference supporting or challenging a claim.
An addressable view of an exact source record ID, version and canonical digest. Resolution reports availability and access status explicitly; current use follows the applicable admission.
A distinct review event or decision over an assertion.
A versioned activity recording how a source or claim representation was produced.
The recorded human, model or system responsibility representation that made a claim.
Root for normalized place identity and claim-scoped spatial references; navigation Regions remain separate.
A persistent normalized Place identity; its names, boundaries and historical validity remain versioned assertions.
An object representing tree or atlas navigation and routes to domain records.
A branch-shaped navigation object in the source tree.
An era route within the atlas, with normalized dating supplied by separate temporal records.
A branch region that organizes navigation; geographic identities and containment use their own source records.
